finding: afterStreamComplete discarded the `ownerPaneId` argument and read the focused-pane bridge (`Chat.$`), so in split view a turn completing in the UNFOCUSED pane loaded the FOCUSED pane's summary — rotating the single-entry store onto the wrong conversation and never refreshing the one that streamed. Both sibling implementations (chat/extensions/text, file/chat-extension) take `ownerPaneId` for exactly this reason and the hook's own doc warns focus is unreliable at this async boundary.
fix: reads `paneRegistry.get(ownerPaneId)?.api.getState()` with the bridge only as a fallback

finding: `createdInThisSession` never expired, but 'provably has no summary' only holds until the conversation's FIRST TURN COMPLETES. After that the open read was suppressed for the rest of the tab session, and because ConversationSummarization is a single-entry cache that rotates on any switch, SummaryBoundaryMarker would go permanently blank for that conversation.
fix: the mark is REMOVED at the end of every turn (applyStreamFrame's completion block); `forgetSessionCreatedConversation` + a test that pins the expiry

finding: Same permanence bug with a worse data path: `releaseConversationScope` DELETES `runsByConversation[id]` on unmount, so navigating away from a session-created conversation and back re-mounted the footer with no cached slice AND no probe; an already-terminal run emits no further `sync:workflow_run`, so the footer (the only route to the Tasks panel) would render nothing for the rest of the session.
fix: same expiry as L-2 — after the first turn completes the conversation probes normally again

finding: The in-flight guard coalesced two reads that want DIFFERENT freshness: if an open read issued before the server wrote is still on the wire when the turn ends, the turn-end read was dropped and the store kept the pre-turn summary with no later trigger to correct it.
fix: `loadForConversation(id, { force: true })` — the turn-end caller always performs its own round-trip (mirrors Auth.refreshCurrentUser's force opt-out)

finding: The marker matched purely on `current.summary.summarized_up_to_id === message.id` with NO conversation guard, so a single-entry store holding another conversation's summary (two split panes; a pane on the new-chat route calling clear()) could attach it to the wrong thread. Pre-existing, but the diff removed the `messages.size` churn that used to mask it.
fix: render only when `current.conversationId === Chat.conversation?.id`

finding: `ensureSessionCreatedTracking` was provably inert: the store's `createConversation` is the sole creation path and marks the id synchronously BEFORE `set({conversation})`, and both `conversation.created` emitters run strictly after that — so the EventBus listener could never mark anything the direct call had missed. It also made the summarization pill's behaviour depend on the background module being in the load wave (blocklistable on desktop).
fix: deleted, along with the background module's `initialize()`; marking stays where the fact is produced and un-marking where it expires

finding: `expect(summaryReads.length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(1)` also passes at ZERO, so a regression that removed the turn-end read entirely — which L-1 makes concretely reachable — would be green.
fix: asserted as `toBe(1)`

finding: TEST-9 drove Enter+Enter only, which `TextInput`'s pre-existing synchronous `inFlightRef` already blocks on the base branch — so the spec passed pre-fix and guarded nothing about the store-level latch. The only entry point that reaches the store latch is the Send BUTTON, whose handler reads rendered state.
fix: added an immediate Send-button click leg after the two Enters, with the reason stated in the spec

finding: The unit test's `readsFor` MODELLED the 'held' derivation as 'the last id read', while the component derives it from `snap.current` / `snap.loading` + `snap.requestedConversationId` — so the one piece of new logic that could actually be wrong was the one piece not covered, including the failed-read case.
fix: extracted `isSummaryHeld(snapshot, id)` as a named pure function, drove `readsFor` through it, and added a direct test for settled / in-flight / wrong-id / FAILED-read

finding: The file header still asserted the pill 'subscribes to messages.size' and carried a 'DO NOT move the trigger elsewhere' warning that the diff falsified; the newly-added SummaryBoundaryMarker comment described the trigger as 'the streaming true→false edge', which the sibling extension.tsx explicitly documents as measured-wrong. Two files added in one change described the mechanism incompatibly.
fix: both headers rewritten; the superseded warning is kept and explained rather than deleted

finding: The skip-link spec cited 'WCAG 2.5.8 minimum 24px' for a KEYBOARD-focused box (2.5.8 governs pointer targets), codified visually-hidden-at-rest as a REQUIREMENT (so making the link permanently visible — a better outcome — would fail), never asserted that activating it MOVES FOCUS (the classic broken-bypass-link failure), and called `#main-content` a landmark when it is a section inside `<main>`.
fix: citation removed and replaced with the repo's own usable-target rationale; hidden-at-rest recorded rather than required; an Enter-activates-and-focus-moves assertion added

finding: The two dynamic `import()`s bought nothing — the extension statically imports the pill, which statically imports both `chatBridge` and `conversationSummarization`, so they are already in the same chunk; they only added two await ticks per completed turn, and the memory-extension rationale they were copied from does not transfer.
fix: converted to static imports

finding: The server's summary refresh is a detached task with its own LLM call, so the turn-end read can land before the write; with `messages.size` gone there is no in-turn retry. ACCEPTED, not fixed: the OLD trigger had the same property (its last message-count change was also the tail reconcile, before the detached task finished), so convergence happened on the next turn or the next conversation switch then, and still does now — the next turn's `afterStreamComplete` re-reads, and a switch away-and-back makes `isSummaryHeld` false. Not a regression; recorded so the next reader does not mistake it for one.
fix: none — rationale recorded here and in the code comment

finding: `afterStreamComplete` is not invoked on the stream ERROR path (`onStreamError`) nor when `applyStreamFrame` takes its `!isOnOriginalConversation` early bail, so those turns get no summary read. ACCEPTED: a turn that errored produced no assistant message, so the server's `after_llm_call` summary hook did not run either — there is nothing new to read; and the switched-away case is repaired by the open read when the user returns (the mark has expired by then only if the turn completed, which is the same condition).
fix: none

finding: A pane on the new-chat route calls `ConversationSummarizationStore.clear()`, wiping a split sibling's loaded summary, and that sibling's effect deps do not change so it never re-reads. Pre-existing consequence of a SINGLE-ENTRY store; the removed `messages.size` churn used to mask it. Mitigated rather than fixed: L-5's conversation guard means the sibling now renders NOTHING instead of the WRONG marker, which is the safe failure. A per-conversation keyed store is the real fix and is out of this round's scope.
fix: partially mitigated by L-5; full fix deferred

finding: `noteSessionCreatedConversation(id: string)` accepts any string, and eviction is FIFO-by-insertion rather than LRU despite the doc saying 'oldest'. ACCEPTED: both failure directions are safe — a wrong id merely marks something nothing reads, and FIFO eviction degrades to probing, which is the pre-change behaviour. The doc wording was left as 'oldest inserted' to match the code.
fix: none

finding: The reviewed diff's latch threw `A message is already being sent`, which the Send-BUTTON path (`ChatInput.handleSend`, no `allowSilentCancel`) would toast to the user for a benign double-click, and used `console.debug` against the repo's §13 rule. NOT APPLICABLE to the shipped branch: `origin/feat/agent-core` advanced to bf1b0e9dd mid-review with its own latch, this branch rebased onto it and dropped its duplicate, so `sendMessage.ts` is byte-identical to upstream and is no longer in the diff. Upstream's variant returns silently for all callers, which does not raise this finding. Recorded for the upstream author.
fix: n/a — file dropped from the diff by the rebase (DRIFT-1.7)

finding: The `zero-size-control` finding is DISPOSITIONED, not eliminated — the audit battery has no sr-only carve-out, so the row will re-fire on every future run. Accepted deliberately: DEC-9 forbids editing the detector during a measurement round (it would invalidate the before→after comparison), and the app-side element is a correct WCAG 2.4.1 bypass link. A carve-out for visually-hidden bypass links is proposed for agent-kit as separate work.
fix: none this round; recorded as a proposed agent-kit tuning

finding: The 'old message-count trigger would have fired four times' case asserts arithmetic over a literal array and touches no production symbol — it is a counter-factual by narration, not by execution. Kept because it documents the defect's magnitude next to the fix, but it is explicitly not load-bearing; the load-bearing counter-factuals are the session-created case (which does drive the real predicate) and the e2e `toBe(1)`.
fix: none — retained as documentation, with the real proof moved to TEST-2

finding: Both specs hand-roll token extraction from localStorage instead of using the existing `getAdminToken(apiURL)` helper the sibling round-1 spec uses. ACCEPTED: the helper takes the API URL and mints a fresh admin token, whereas these specs need the token of the session the page is already logged into (they assert on that session's requests); reading it from the page is the correct source here.
fix: none
